notes.gdp: GDP is Eurostat's quarterly national accounts, seasonally and calendar adjusted. Figures before the euro's launch in 1999 are converted from Luxembourg francs at the fixed rate of 40.3399 francs per euro.
notes.inflation: Inflation is the EU's harmonised index (HICP), the measure the ECB targets; STATEC also publishes a national CPI, which can differ by a few tenths. Luxembourg has used the euro since its launch on 1 January 1999 and has had no policy rate of its own since: the rate shown is the European Central Bank's deposit facility rate. Before 1999 the Luxembourg franc was at par with the Belgian franc, in a monetary association with Belgium.
notes.labour: Unemployment is Eurostat's monthly, seasonally adjusted rate (ILO definition, ages 15 to 74). ADEM's registered unemployment, sometimes quoted in Luxembourg news, is a different measure. Employment and participation rates are Eurostat's seasonally adjusted Labour Force Survey figures for ages 15 to 64, from 2009. They cover residents only, while a large share of the people working in Luxembourg commute from neighbouring countries.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Eurostat's monthly total with the rest of the world, in euros. Luxembourg usually imports more goods than it exports; most of its exports are services, which are not shown here.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are Eurostat's excessive deficit procedure figures for general government, calendar years, so the latest year is a year ahead of the IMF's.
notes.markets: The 10-year yield is the OECD's monthly series for Luxembourg government bonds, via FRED, from 1993; it matches Eurostat's convergence rate. The exchange rates are the Federal Reserve's daily euro rates, shared with every euro area page. Business confidence is the OECD's indicator, where 100 is the long-run average.
